annotations.description: Playing Plains instead of Island on turn 1 means they cannot hold up Brainstorm, the only 1-mana instant in their hand. Having Island available allows casting Brainstorm at end of an opponent's turn to dig for better cards and set up future draws.

annotations.betterLine: Play Island to hold up Brainstorm on turn 1, maximizing the ability to dig through the deck early and find additional lands or key spells.

annotations.description: Howling Mine is a symmetrical draw effect that benefits all four opponents equally. In a 4-player game, you draw 1 extra card per turn cycle but your opponents collectively draw 3 extra cards. This is especially bad when played early (turn 3) as it accelerates opponents into their threats and answers. Meanwhile, Jotun Grunt is a 4/4 for 2 mana that applies pressure and can manage graveyards. Additionally, Gem3F Stoic already has a Baleful Strix on board that benefits from extra cards, and DSV3 Spike has Jet Medallion to cast cheaper spells drawn off the Mine.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Howling Mine, giving all opponents extra draws
annotations.betterLine: Cast Jotun Grunt as a 4/4 body for 2 mana to apply early pressure and control graveyards, rather than giving opponents card advantage with Howling Mine

annotations.description: Casting Skirsdag High Priest first instead of Mind Stone. While both could potentially be cast this turn (total 3 mana needed, 4 available), Mind Stone should be the priority to ensure mana ramp toward Drana on turn 4. Skirsdag High Priest is nearly useless without other creatures and morbid, making it a very low-impact play on its own. If for some reason only one spell gets cast, Mind Stone is clearly better.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Skirsdag High Priest
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mind Stone first to secure ramp toward turn 4 Drana, then cast Skirsdag High Priest with remaining mana if desired.

annotations.description: DSV3 Spike has 5 lands (including Jet Medallion for cost reduction) and Mind Stone in hand, but chose to pass without playing anything. Mind Stone costs 2 mana and would provide ramp for the expensive cards in hand (Drana at 5 mana, Evernight Shade at 4 mana, Skeletal Scrying). With only 4 lands producing mana plus Jet Medallion, deploying Mind Stone accelerates toward casting Drana or Syr Konrad-level threats a turn earlier. Swiftfoot Boots (also 2 mana) could also be deployed to protect a future Drana. There's no reason to hold mana open with no instants worth casting at this point in the game (Skeletal Scrying with X=0 is useless, and Black Sun's Zenith for X=0 or X=1 isn't needed yet).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting any spells, leaving mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mind Stone (2 mana) to ramp toward Drana or Evernight Shade next turn, or cast Swiftfoot Boots to prepare for protecting Drana when she comes down.

annotations.description: Cycling Miscalculation instead of making a land drop on Turn 3 with an extremely mana-hungry hand (Damnation, Cryptic Command, Mystical Teachings, Sylvan Library). Missing land drops delays all these powerful spells.

annotations.description: Gem3F Stoic has Krosan Grip in hand and MiMo Vorthos has Howling Mine on the battlefield, which benefits all opponents equally. Destroying Howling Mine with Krosan Grip (which has split second, so it can't be responded to) would deny card advantage to all three opponents while Stoic already has a strong hand with Damnation, Cryptic Command, Mystical Teachings, and Miscalculation. Instead, they chose to cast Sylvan Library, which is a strong card but could have been played next turn after removing Howling Mine. However, Sylvan Library is excellent and playing it early maximizes its value over time, and Howling Mine does also give Stoic extra draws. The decision is defensible but debatable - Howling Mine helping three opponents vs. one player is generally bad for the table, and Stoic already has a full hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sylvan Library instead of using Krosan Grip on Howling Mine
annotations.betterLine: Cast Krosan Grip targeting Howling Mine to deny card advantage to all three opponents, then play Sylvan Library next turn for personal card advantage

annotations.description: Goblin Cadets is a 2/1 for R with the significant downside that whenever it blocks or becomes blocked, an opponent gains control of it. In a multiplayer game, this creature is almost always a liability - it can't attack profitably into any board with blockers without giving itself away, and it can't block without the same problem. Meanwhile, Soul Snare (W enchantment that can exile an attacking creature) provides defensive value, and Windborn Muse (3W flying 2/3 that taxes attackers) would be castable next turn and provides much better board presence. Crescendo of War (3W) is also available and could be impactful. Playing a creature that will likely be given away to an opponent seems low-value compared to deploying Soul Snare for 1 mana, which provides immediate defensive utility.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Goblin Cadets (R) in postcombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Cast Soul Snare (W) instead, which provides actual defensive value without the risk of giving an opponent a creature. Soul Snare can exile an attacking creature targeting you or your planeswalker, offering real protection.

annotations.description: Ob Nixilis is at 3 loyalty and using -2 brings it to 1 loyalty, making it very vulnerable. The +2 ability would bring it to 5 loyalty (much safer) while draining 3 life from opponents (1 each from 3 opponents) and gaining 3 life. DSV3 Spike already has a decent board with Skirsdag High Priest and other creatures in hand. With Howling Mine giving extra draws, protecting the planeswalker for repeated value over multiple turns could be more impactful than a single 5/5 demon token that costs 2 life. However, a 5/5 flyer is a significant threat in multiplayer, and it enables Skirsdag High Priest's morbid-related synergies and provides a sacrifice target for Infernal Offering in hand. The decision is defensible but the loyalty risk is real.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Ob Nixilis -2 to create a 5/5 Demon token with flying, dropping to 1 loyalty and losing 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Use +2 to drain opponents for 3 total life, gain 3 life, and protect Ob Nixilis at 5 loyalty. This preserves the planeswalker for future activations and incremental advantage, especially with multiple creatures already in hand to deploy.

With DSV3 Spike having Ob Nixilis capable of making 5/5 demons, and MiMo Vorthos having Jotun Grunt, Gem3F Stoic at 19 life could take significant damage. Gem3F Stoic has Miscalculation in hand which could counter Kardur unless the opponent pays {2}. Gem3P Johnny has only Foreboding Ruins untapped (and Swamp and Mountain untapped), so after casting Kardur for {2}{B}{R} using Temple of the False God + Mountain + Foreboding Ruins + Mountain/Swamp, they likely have limited mana remaining. Looking at Gem3P Johnny's board: Mountain (tapped), Swamp (untapped), Mountain (untapped), Temple of the False God (tapped), Foreboding Ruins (tapped), Rakdos Signet. They cast Kardur for BBRR using some combination. They may have 1-2 mana available to pay for Miscalculation. However, Cryptic Command is also available and cannot be paid around - it would counter Kardur and draw a card. Gem3F has the mana: Underground Sea + Tropical Island + Snow-Covered Island + Island = UUUB or similar, enough for {1}{U}{U}{U}. Letting Kardur resolve when at 19 life with a forced-attack effect is very dangerous.

annotations.betterLine: Counter Kardur with Cryptic Command (counter + draw) or at minimum attempt Miscalculation. Kardur's forced-attack effect is extremely threatening at 19 life, especially with other players having board presence that will be forced to swing at Gem3F Stoic.
